title: Cut elimination for propositional sequents

based_on.title: Proof Theory: Foundations and Applications (June 2013 lecture notes)
based_on.pages: Section 1.3 pp. 9–15; auxiliary/principal reductions and the contraction issue pp. 10–12; source gives a reducibility alternative. One-sided specialization from section 1.2 Exercise 4.

summary: Eliminate intermediate cuts by explicit transformations of finite propositional proof trees, then obtain subformula and consistency consequences.
abstract: A proof often uses an intermediate lemma that disappears from its final statement. In a sequent calculus, the cut rule expresses this way of composing two arguments. We show that every finite propositional proof using cut can be rebuilt without it. The construction first exposes the parts of compound formulas and replaces opposite literals, then composes arguments by induction on the size of their intermediate formula. The resulting proof uses only subformulas of its conclusion. This gives a syntactic explanation of why neither an empty set of alternatives nor falsity alone has a proof, while allowing an original proof to contain unrelated intermediate formulas.
